Senses.Explanation: To appraise and distinguish is to test, sort, or discriminate people, responses, or stated teaching positions. To appraise, sort out, or distinguish; noun constructions name the resulting appraisal or classificatory distinction. The term is attested 266 times in 126 allowlisted texts. Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu's unnamed questioner sets two episodes side by side and asks Nanyue to “please appraise and distinguish” them (兩段不同，試請料揀); Wuyi Yuanlai asks who can sort out a presented conjunction. The same appraisal vocabulary appears in Linji's “Four Selections” (四料揀). The Eye of Humans and Gods records Nanyuan Huiyong asking Fengxue Yanzhao, “the Four Selections—what do the selections select?” (四料揀，料揀何法), and compiler Huiyan Zhizhao begins another exposition with people of middle and lower capacity under that heading. Zhanran Yuancheng calls paired evaluative formulas “the old so-called selection sayings” (古所謂料揀語). The public act, resulting distinction, and named set remain one appraisal-and-selection family; noun and verb grammar alone do not create different lexical things.

Senses.Explanation: A person hangs in a tree with the mouth gripping the only supporting branch: neither hand holds a branch and neither foot rests on one. Xiangyan Zhixian's setup places an unnamed person below who asks the meaning of the ancestral teacher's coming from the west. Refusing to answer fails the question, but speaking means releasing the mouth's sole hold and losing one's life. Xiangyan's physical predicament becomes the named 'Xiangyan up the tree' public case. Zhean Jingfan preserves Hutou's counter-question about before the ascent; an impersonal heading numbers and titles the case in Wansong Xingxiu's commentary; Yulin Tongxiu raises it as a public case; Dahui Zonggao examines an unnamed monk with it in an entering interview; a reviewed unnamed monk asks Zongbao Daodu about it and Zongbao answers; and Lingyin Jude Li raises it to test Miaoyun before pressing the before-ascent question. The headword names this case and testing history, not Xiangyan as a separate dictionary figure.
